question: Which statement best describes Single source of truth?
options: When lifting state, move it only to the nearest ancestor that renders all the components needing it — not higher. The common parent is the lowest component in the tree that contains every consumer. Lifting higher than necessary causes wasted re-renders and prop-drilling through layers that don't use the value, so finding the right level is the whole skill.

Lifting state up establishes one authoritative place where a piece of data lives, so the UI can never display two conflicting versions of it. When siblings each keep their own copy, they inevitably drift out of sync and produce bugs like a count showing 3 in one place and 2 in another. By owning the value in a common parent, you guarantee every consumer reads the same truth.

The default should be to keep state as low as possible (colocated) in the component that uses it, because it re-renders less and stays self-contained. Lift it up only when another component, especially a sibling, genuinely needs to read or change the same value. The rule of thumb: colocate until sharing forces you to lift — don't lift preemptively 'to be safe'.

Because React data flows one way, parents pass the current value down to children as props and pass functions down so children can request changes. The child never mutates the value directly — it calls the callback with the new value and the parent updates its state. This keeps the data flow explicit and traceable, since you can always see who owns a value and who can change it.

question: Which statement best describes Props down, callbacks up?

If a value can be computed from existing state, derive it during render rather than storing it in its own state. Duplicating a derived value (like a result count) into separate state invites drift, because you have to remember to update it everywhere. Computing it from the single shared source on each render keeps it automatically correct.

This is the wrong fix for duplicated state — it adds an extra render, can cause subtle timing bugs, and hides the real problem. question: Which statement best describes Colocation vs lifting?
options: Lifting state works beautifully until the value must reach many deeply nested components, at which point you end up prop-drilling — threading the same props through intermediate components that don't use them. That's the signal to graduate to Context, which lets distant components subscribe to shared state directly without manual prop threading. For very large or widely shared state, a store like Redux or Zustand is the next step.

question: Which statement best describes Derived values vs duplicated state?
options: The component that owns lifted state re-renders on every change, and so do the children it passes new props to. Lifting too high therefore re-renders large subtrees needlessly on each update. Mitigate by lifting only as high as necessary, splitting big components into smaller ones, and wrapping pure children in React.memo so they skip re-renders when their props are unchanged.
